# hermestrator

> Automated GitHub ticket implementation on top of [swamp](https://github.com/swamp-club/swamp)
> and [ralphex](https://github.com/umputun/ralphex). A poller finds issues in
> *other* repositories that are labeled `agent-ready` and already carry a
> committed plan, then a worker runs a coding agent (Codex or Pi) against that
> plan and opens a pull request — all inside a container hermestrator builds
> and owns. This file is for an agent working in one of those *other*
> repositories that wants to be picked up by hermestrator.

This is not hermestrator's own contributor doc (see AGENTS.md/README.md for
that). It's the contract a target repo must satisfy from the outside — no
access to hermestrator's source required.

## What hermestrator needs from your repo

Nothing, by default — a repo with no `scripts/agent-setup.sh` and no special
config still works, ralphex just runs against whatever's on the base image.
Add the pieces below only if your repo needs them.

1. **A plan on a specific branch.** hermestrator never invents work. Someone
   (a human, or an agent using the `hermestrator-plan` skill) must:
   - open or reuse issue `#N`,
   - create branch `agent/issue-<N>` off your default branch,
   - commit exactly one plan file under `docs/plans/*.md` on that branch
     (ralphex's own working format — task list ralphex executes step by
     step), push it,
   - label issue `#N` with `agent-ready`.
   The poller only triggers on `agent-ready` issues that have this branch
   with this plan already pushed — it does not write plans itself.
2. **Optional: an `agent-pi` or `agent-codex` label** on the issue to route
   to a specific coding agent. No label uses hermestrator's configured
   default (currently `ralphex-codex`).
3. **Optional: `scripts/agent-setup.sh`** in your repo root — see below. Only
   needed if your repo requires install/build steps before lint/test/build
   commands work in a fresh checkout.
4. **A GitHub owner hermestrator is already configured for.** hermestrator
   authenticates per-owner with a fine-grained PAT (`GH_TOKEN_<OWNER>`); an
   unmapped owner fails loudly rather than silently reusing another owner's
   token. If your repo's owner isn't already onboarded, that's a
   hermestrator-side change, not something your repo can do alone — ask
   whoever operates the hermestrator instance.

## The run, end to end

```
issue #N gets `agent-ready` + agent/issue-N branch with a plan
        │
        ▼
poller (cron, ~15m): finds it, has no open PR yet, no run already in flight
        │  triggers
        ▼
worker: clone target repo @ agent/issue-N into a fresh /tmp workspace
        → run scripts/agent-setup.sh if present+executable
        → ralphex <plan-file> --base-ref <default-branch> --branch agent/issue-N
        → ralphex commits, archives the plan to docs/plans/completed/ or
          docs/plans/archive/, and moves on
        → push agent/issue-N, open or update the PR, remove agent-ready
```

A follow-up round on the same issue is just: push a new `docs/plans/*.md` to
the same branch and re-add `agent-ready` — the worker pushes into the
existing PR (or opens a new one if it was closed/merged) instead of starting
over.

Every run starts from an empty clone — nothing is cached, no state persists
in your repo between runs except what you commit.

## `scripts/agent-setup.sh` contract

The worker image intentionally ships **no language runtimes** beyond
`mise` (https://mise.jdx.dev) — it doesn't hardcode any repo's toolchain.
If your repo needs anything installed before its lint/test/typecheck/build
commands work, provide this script; if not, skip it entirely (no file = no-op,
the worker doesn't fail or warn).

Requirements:

- `#!/usr/bin/env bash` + `set -Eeuo pipefail`, `chmod +x`.
- Pin exact tool versions in this repo's own `mise.toml`/`.mise.toml`
  (e.g. `bun = "x.y.z"`) and run `mise install` first. Everything the script
  and the coding agent run afterward must resolve those exact binaries, not
  whatever happens to already be on `PATH`.
  `mise install` does **not** update the parent shell — a subprocess can't
  push tools onto the PATH of the worker process that runs this script.
  Two ways to make the resolved tools available beyond this script's own
  process:
  - run everything needing them through `mise exec -- <command>` inside this
    script (each invocation re-resolves per-project tools), or
  - `mise activate`/shim it so mise's own shims dir is what later processes
    pick up (this is how hermestrator's own worker image handles its
    Swift/mise toolchain — see its `worker/Dockerfile` for the pattern:
    mise shims placed first on `PATH` in the image's own environment).
  Either way, don't assume a plain `export PATH=...` inside this script
  reaches ralphex or the coding agent afterward — this script runs as a
  subprocess of the worker, its `export`s don't propagate to siblings/parent.
- Install this repo's dependencies with whatever package manager/tooling this
  repo already uses — don't introduce a new one. Prefer one top-level command
  over per-directory installs if your tooling supports it (monorepos: cover
  every workspace/service that has a validation gate).
- If a client-side git hook (pre-commit, pre-push) gates lint/typecheck/test
  in this repo, make it mandatory here: after install, verify the hook file
  exists and is executable, exit non-zero if not. A coding agent silently
  committing past a missing gate is worse than the setup script failing
  loudly.
- After install, cheaply sanity-check that the commands CI/pre-commit
  actually rely on resolve (e.g. `--version` on the lint/test binaries, or
  this repo's own `check` command); exit non-zero if something didn't
  resolve. Don't leave a half-set-up workspace to fail silently deeper into
  the agent's run.
- Only what lint/test/typecheck/build actually need — no unrelated build
  steps (native mobile builds, docs builds, container builds, etc.).
- Match what this repo's own CI or pre-commit hooks already run. Don't invent
  new tooling or commands that don't already exist somewhere in the repo.
- Minimal comments — this is a small infra script, not documentation.

## Producing the plan

If you're an agent (not a human) preparing an issue for hermestrator, use the
`hermestrator-plan` skill if it's available in your environment — it turns
`gh issue view <N>` into the branch/plan/label sequence above, including
running the plan through review before pushing. Otherwise, replicate Step 1-6
of that skill by hand: branch `agent/issue-<N>` off default, one plan file
in `docs/plans/`, push, label `agent-ready` (+ optional `agent-pi`/
`agent-codex`).
